insider_note: Two facts and a definition that must include 'internodes'. One line each.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What bolting is
steps.margin_note: Definition with internodes and the timing. One example helps.
lines: Bolting is the sudden ELONGATION OF
It is seen in rosette plants such as cabbage and
beet, whose internodes are normally very short.
steps.why: A rosette plant has almost no visible stem, so the sudden elongation before flowering is dramatic and easy to name.
common_mistakes: Saying bolting is the growth of roots. It is INTERNODE elongation.
Leaving out 'just before flowering'. The timing is part of the definition.
steps.memory_tip: The stem shoots up right before the flower opens.

steps.label: The hormone
steps.margin_note: Name the hormone and link it to the elongation effect.
lines: This is the same elongation effect that lengthens
steps.why: Bolting is internode elongation, and internode elongation is what gibberellin does everywhere else in the chapter, so it is the same effect under a different name.
common_mistakes: Naming auxin. Bolting is a GIBBERELLIN effect.
Naming no hormone. Half the question is the hormone.
steps.memory_tip: Anything that gets longer is gibberellin.
